# Longhorn backend (first integration slice)

Atlas can discover Longhorn v1beta2 `nodes` and `volumes` through the Kubernetes API. Enable it
with `ATLAS_LONGHORN_ENABLE=1` and, if needed, `ATLAS_LONGHORN_NAMESPACE=longhorn-system`.
Configure the gateway service account with read access to those CRDs; the included
`deploy/k8s/atlas-gateway.yaml` role contains the permission. The gateway fails startup if the
Kubernetes client cannot initialize. Run `POST /api/atlas/v1/backends/bkd_longhorn/discover`
after Longhorn is installed. Failed CRD reads fail discovery; no demo data is substituted.

The backend shows physical node-disk capacity, volume sizes, PVC identity and Longhorn robustness.
Unknown disk capacity is reported as unknown. Its one synthetic `longhorn` pool aggregates disks;
it does not represent a Longhorn replica placement or disk pool. Ceph OSD, CephFS and RGW
operations do not apply. The native driver is read-only.

Atlas can create a Longhorn PVC using its existing Kubernetes job path. Supply both the Atlas
backend ID and a StorageClass whose provisioner is `driver.longhorn.io`:

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "your-tenant-id",
  "name": "app-data",
  "size_bytes": 10737418240,
  "kind": "block",
  "kubernetes": {
    "backend_id": "bkd_longhorn",
    "namespace": "default",
    "storage_class": "longhorn"
  }
}
```

Send this to `POST /api/atlas/v1/volumes` with the usual Atlas authorization. An explicit
Longhorn StorageClass is required: the default policy catalog still resolves to Ceph classes.
Atlas checks the actual StorageClass provisioner and the backend's cordon state before queuing.
Snapshot/clone, Longhorn backup, replica placement, and native volume mutations are not implemented
by this driver. Validate RWX migration on your chosen Longhorn storage mode before using it for
KubeVirt live migration.
